covers.quote: Writing to an Australian year 7 level makes content usable for most people.
Level AAA requires a lower secondary education reading level, after removal of proper names and titles (year 7 or between 12 and 14 years old).

rules.quote: Check that your content is a reading level 2 (Australian year 7 equivalent).
rules.specification: The readability of the text, after removal of proper names and titles, should correspond to an Australian Year 7 reading level (or approximately ages 12–14).
rules.violation_condition: content exceeds an Australian year 7 reading level (reading level 2 / lower secondary education reading level)
when: Specialist content for technical users should also be written in plain language, but general content must be accessible to everyone.
rules.why: G-1, G-4: Core target reading level requirement for content on this page, consolidating mentions across introductory text, WCAG summary, and recommendations.

rules.quote: Avoid (or explain) unusual words, phrases, idioms and so on.
rules.specification: Avoid idioms, colloquial phrases, or uncommon/unusual terminology unless immediately explained in plain language.
rules.violation_condition: text contains unusual words, idioms, or uncommon phrases without an accompanying explanation
when: Unusual words or phrases are permissible if they are explicitly explained.
rules.why: E-2: Direct rule listed under accessibility fundamentals corresponding to WCAG 3.1.3.

rules.quote: Expand all acronyms on their first use.
rules.violation_condition: an acronym is used for the first time without its full expansion provided
rules.why: Direct rule under accessibility requirements on acronym expansions (WCAG 3.1.4).

rules.violation_condition: a sentence uses two negative words or phrases that negate each other
rules.why: Clear stylistic requirement listed under accessibility requirements.
